messages:
jasmin: Heads-up — we saw a flood of SLO notifications during the canary rollout around 11:05. Seems like per-tenant quiet windows didn't suppress fanout to the oncall channel. Anyone else see this?
lee: saw it, yep. lots of duplicates. Might be mapping mismatch between notify-policy and console routing. :grimacing:
alan: is the issue notify API emitting separate alerts per tenant even when quiet window is active?
maria: my quick read — notify-service checks quiet-window at emit-time, but fanout happens in notify-worker which currently trusts the routing table snapshot cached earlier. If snapshot stale -> fanout occurs.
jasmin: exact. root cause is a 2m cache TTL on routing metadata. Canary changed policy labels, cache not invalidated.
tom: oof. so two pieces: cache TTL and notify-worker respect for quiet windows. Which do we prioritize? quick fix vs long-term API change?
lee: quick fix = invalidate cache on policy rollout + emergency backpressure in worker. long-term = move quiet-window check into fanout path so worker double-checks at send-time.
alan: agree. but moving check into fanout touches notify API contract (workers must be able to query console metadata). That's an internal API change, needs versioning.
maria: +1. also telemetry gap: we had no per-tenant fanout telemetry in the pipeline, so it was hard to tell how many tenants got noisy alerts. We should add a counter labeled by tenant_id and policy_id.
jasmin: adding counters sounds low-risk. Can we do that in the worker and emit to the existing alerts metric stream?
lee: yes. patch would be tiny: increment before send and tag with tenant+policy. Then dashboards can filter.
tom: for the cache TTL, emergency fix: set TTL=15s for policy entries and deploy a rolling restart of notify-worker. Risky but acceptable for 30m window.
alan: rolling restart is fine. ops: be careful with burst traffic if we invalidate caches simultaneously. add jitter.
maria: putting a small snippet of what I'm thinking for the fanout guard (pseudo):
```
// worker send path
if (routingSnapshot.isStale()) fetchLatest()
if (tenantInQuietWindow(tenant_id)) skipSend()
emit_metric("notify.fanout.send", {tenant:tenant_id, policy:policy_id, outcome: 'skipped|sent'})
```
jasmin: that looks good. two questions: 1) how do we signal to console UI that an alert was suppressed vs delivered? 2) do we want a fallback routing tier (low-priority) instead of skip?
lee: UI signal: add field `delivery_status` to alert events: "skipped_quiet_window", "sent_low_priority", "sent_normal". Consumers (console + billing) can handle. That's an API addition but additive.
alan: fallback tier feels like product decision. For now implement skipped + metrics, iterate.
maria: agree. also add a sampling flag to avoid exploding metrics during incidents: sample rate = min(1, 1000 / qps) as a safety.
tom: rollout plan: 1) metrics in worker (safe) 2) short TTL and cache invalidation on policy update (emergency) 3) fanout double-check and delivery_status (API v2, doced) 4) UI changes + dashboards. Anyone object?
lee: fine. timeline?
jasmin: can we do 1+2 in next 3 hours? ops ready for restart? @lee you good to cut the restart?
lee: yep. I'll coordinate with oncall, will add 30-60s jitter per pod and ramp.
maria: I'll open a tiny PR for metrics and add testing.
alan: I'll draft API docs for delivery_status and versioning notes.
redwood-alerts-bot: Deploy bot: notify-worker rollout started by lee at 2023-10-11T11:30:12Z (canary pods first). :rocket:
jasmin: thanks. After metrics are in, can we add a dashboard panel: fanout_count by delivery_status + per-tenant spike detector? Need to spot regressions quickly.
maria: yep I'll add to the notify-service dashboard. Use burn-rate style alert if skipped/sent ratio jumps > 0.1 in 5m.
tom: one more thing — quota interplay: if tenant is at notify quota, worker currently drops silently. We should surface "dropped_quota" as a delivery_status too so console shows quota hits.
lee: good catch. add that to the list.
jasmin: summary: emergency TTL drop+restart, metrics tagging, API field for delivery_status, later fanout double-check + UI updates, surface quota drops. Thanks all, will file followups. :thumbsup:
